# Conversation Summary - 2026-03-30

**Summary:** Enhanced Hot Money Radar with full profile modal, local LLM integration (Qwen 2.5 & Llama 3.1), and AI-powered profile pulling. Added Paste Deal feature with smart text extraction and Obsidian integration.

**Topics:** Hot Money Radar, Profile Modal, Local LLM Integration, Qwen 2.5, Llama 3.1, Deal Parsing, Obsidian Export, Profile Intelligence

**Decisions:**
- Use local LLM (Llama 3.1 8B) for fast deal extraction and profiling
- Qwen 2.5 14B available for advanced reasoning tasks
- Profiles save to Obsidian: `Deals/Profiles/Profile_-_Entity_Name.md`
- Smart paste auto-extracts: entity, cash, property type, location, dates
- Cards are fully clickable for better UX

**Action Items:**
- [ ] Test LLM profile pulling with real entities
- [ ] Add more sophisticated web scraping for profile enrichment
- [ ] Consider vector search for similar deal matching
- [ ] Add email/phone extraction from web search

**Files Changed:**

**Frontend:**
- `nerve/src/views/HotMoneyRadar.jsx` - Added LeadDetailModal, PasteDealModal, Profile Intelligence section, clickable cards

**Backend:**
- `api_server.py` - Added:
  - `/api/hotmoney/*` - Full CRUD for hot money leads
  - `/api/hotmoney/stats` - Statistics endpoint
  - `/api/llm/status` - LLM health check
  - `/api/llm/generate` - Text generation
  - `/api/llm/chat` - Chat completion
  - `/api/llm/extract-deal` - Smart deal parsing
  - `/api/llm/pull-profile` - AI profile research
  - `/api/obsidian/quick-link` - Obsidian note creation

**Database:**
- `hot_money_leads` table with: entity, cash_amount, property_type, asset_class, address, contacts (JSON), notes

**Features Implemented:**
1. Full profile modal with editable fields (entity, cash, asset class, property details, contacts, notes)
2. Auto-generated quick links (Google, LinkedIn, Corporation, Realtor.ca)
3. Smart Paste Deal - paste any text, AI extracts structured data
4. Profile Intelligence - AI researches entity and generates profile
5. Obsidian integration - deals and profiles auto-save to vault
6. Clickable cards - entire lead card opens profile
7. Database persistence - all data saved to SQLite

**Local LLM Models Available:**
- `llama3.1:8b` - Default, fast (20s), good for extraction
- `qwen2.5:14b` - 14.8B params, slower, advanced reasoning
- `deepseek-r1:8b` - Code/math tasks
- `re-analyst:latest` - 1.2B, very fast property analysis

**Session ID:** session_2026-03-28_14:53:39

### 1. Recruiter Database Rebuild ✅
Rebuilt entire recruiter database from DBeaver exports with actual cities/regions

**Stats:**
- Total Agents: 96,265 (up from 28,505)
- Unique Cities: 93
- Unique Brokerages: 2978
- Top City: Toronto (37,624)

- Joined realtor_brokers + realtor_salespersons with realtor_brokerages
- Real city data: 93 unique cities across Ontario
- Proper quick links generated for all 96,265 agents

### 2. Frontend Routing Fix ✅
Fixed EXP Agent Recruiter not displaying and city filter returning 0 results

- App.jsx now routes to EXAgentRecruiterUpdated instead of old component
- City dropdown searches across all agent fields instead of exact city match
- JSON fallback when API server is offline
- Added 500/page pagination option

Fixed SQLite FTS5 search breaking on special characters in city names

Same DBeaver join → SQLite → JSON → Frontend pattern applies to all data types

- Builders (companys_final.csv + company_contacts_final.csv)
- Buyers (sale_agents_final.csv)
- Sellers (sale_agents_final.csv)

- Lenders (lenders_final.csv + lender_contacts_final.csv)

**Steps:**
- 1. Identify the DBeaver CSV files for the entity type
- 2. Join parent/child tables on foreign keys (e.g., broker_id)
- 3. Generate quick links for each record
- 4. Create/update SQLite table with proper indexes and FTS5
- 5. Export lean JSON to nerve/public/data/ for frontend fallback
- 6. Update/create frontend view component
- 7. Add API endpoints in api_server.py
- 8. Wire up routing in nerve/src/App.jsx

```bash

python3 rebuild_recruiters_from_dbeaver.py

# Start API server

# Build frontend
cd nerve && npm run build
```

- api_base: http://localhost:8000/api
